questions.help: Safe driving      7 Driving on iceWhen there is the presence of ice on the road, drivers should adopt the same precaution as travelling on snow. This means that, similar to snow, there is a risk of sliding and skidding. Always operate the hand controls and foot controls smoothly.Turn the steering wheel, gently as it is particularly sensitive and the steering will feel very light when driving on ice. This is because there is reduced grip (adhesion) between the tyres and icy road surface. Smoothly and progressively, operate the clutch, accelerator and brake.  It is better to raise the foot slowly off the accelerator in a bid to lose speed. Try to avoid using the brakes, and always brake gently where necessary, so as not to lose control of the car.  (Página 230 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help: 11 Crash helmets   11.1 Tips for buying a crash helmet Visors:Visors are strongly recommended. However, it is important to ensure that these do not mist up; therefore, special covers are available that increase the anti-mist properties. When the helmet does not include eye protection it is highly recommended that safety glasses are used, although this use is not mandatory. Without eye protection, there is obviously the risk that something may enter the eye (an insect, a particle of sand or dust, etc.,) which may cause the rider to become distracted; however, the cold and/or the wind constantly in the eyes also increases visual fatigue.(Página 82 del manual 'Learning to drive')Safe driving    11 The sunThe sun can cause dazzle and discomfort to the drivers of vehicles.The suns rays directly (or indirectly) reflect off surfaces particularly shinny surfaces, such as windows, mirrors, cars etc. and also off of wet road surfaces.In order to protect from this intense light and glare it is advisable to:Keep all windows clean (refracted light can cause more discomfort).Utilise the sun visor(s) and turn them to the most suitable angle.Wear sunglasses (but only during the day and never at night or in tunnels.(Página 233 del manual 'Learning to drive')
